summary: Taipei Songshan International Airport (TSA) is a major urban airport situated just minutes from downtown Taipei in the Songshan District, offering one of the most convenient airport-to-city transfers of any major Asian capital. Originally established as a Japanese military aerodrome in the 1930s, it now serves as Taipei's primary hub for domestic flights and short-haul international routes to mainland China, Japan, and South Korea. The airport shares its grounds with an active Republic of China Air Force base, a unique dual-use arrangement reflecting its long military heritage.
faqs:
Q: How far is Taipei Songshan Airport from the city center?
A: Songshan Airport is remarkably close to central Taipei, roughly 3-5 km from the main business and shopping districts, making it one of the most accessible urban airports in Asia.

Q: Which airlines operate from Taipei Songshan Airport?
A: TSA primarily serves domestic Taiwanese carriers like UNI Air and Mandarin Airlines, along with regional international flights operated by China Airlines, EVA Air, Japan Airlines, ANA, China Eastern, and XiamenAir among others.

Q: Does Taipei Songshan Airport have an MRT station?
A: Yes, the airport is directly served by the Songshan Airport MRT Station on the Wenhu (Brown) Line, which connects to Taipei's broader metro network including links to Taipei Main Station.

Q: Can I take a direct flight from Songshan to other Asian cities?
A: Songshan operates direct flights to several Asian destinations including Tokyo (Haneda), Seoul, Shanghai (Hongqiao), Beijing, and various other mainland Chinese and Japanese cities.
transport_tips: The Wenhu (Brown) Line MRT is the fastest and most affordable way to reach central Taipei, with Songshan Airport Station connected directly to the terminal. Taxis are plentiful and inexpensive by international standards, with a trip to most central Taipei hotels typically taking 15-25 minutes depending on traffic. For travelers heading to other parts of Taiwan, the airport is well-connected to major highways and is closer to the city than Taipei Railway Station.
